classification.difficultyReason: Choose addition or subtraction of squares from the table columns; supplied hypotenuse and leg roles scaffold the routine procedure.

inlines.text: In the table below, the side lengths of right-angled triangles are listed. Complete the table, giving answers as a whole number or square root.
Lengths of the two shortest sides of a right-angled triangle
Lengths of the two shortest sides of a right-angled triangle

answer.worked:
Use $c^2=a^2+b^2$ for the hypotenuse and subtract a squared leg to find a shorter side.

a $c=\sqrt{3^2+4^2}=5\text{ cm}$.

b $c=\sqrt{5^2+6^2}=\sqrt{61}\text{ cm}$.

c $b=\sqrt{9^2-4^2}=\sqrt{65}\text{ cm}$.

d $c=\sqrt{6^2+10^2}=\sqrt{136}\text{ cm}$.

e $a=\sqrt{10^2-7^2}=\sqrt{51}\text{ cm}$.
